rules.construct: A comparison: `a < b`, `x == y`, `key in table`.
rules.condition: A comparison uses exactly one comparison operator. Chained comparisons such as `a < b < c` are not permitted.

rules.construct: Template string literals (PEP 750): `t"Hello {name}"`.
rules.replacement: Use an f-string to build text. To escape or quote values, call the escaping function explicitly on each value.

rules.construct: A conditional expression: `a if condition else b`.
rules.condition: The test and both branches of a conditional expression do not contain another conditional expression.

rules.construct: Starred expressions: `f(*args)`, `[*head, *tail]`, `first, *rest = items`.
rules.condition: A starred expression may unpack values into a call or a list, tuple, or set display. It must not be an assignment target or a `for` loop target.

rules.construct: Anonymous functions: `lambda item: item.size`.
rules.condition: A lambda is permitted only as a direct argument of a call, such as `sorted(items, key=lambda item: item.size)`.

rules.construct: List, set, and dict comprehensions, generator expressions, and their `for` / `if` clauses.
rules.condition: A comprehension has exactly one `for` clause and at most one `if` clause, and contains no other comprehension.

rules.construct: Assignment expressions (the walrus operator): `(match := pattern.search(line))`.
rules.replacement: Assign the value in its own statement on the line before, then use the name.

rules.construct: Assignment: `total = 0`, `x, y = point`.
rules.condition: An assignment has exactly one target, before a single `=`. Chained assignment such as `a = b = 0` is not permitted. Unpacking into one tuple target such as `x, y = point` is permitted.

rules.construct: The `global` and `nonlocal` declarations.
rules.replacement: Pass the value in as an argument and return the new value. To keep shared state, put it in an object that is passed explicitly.

rules.construct: An `else` clause on a `for` or `while` loop.
rules.replacement: Record the outcome in a variable inside the loop, then test that variable after the loop with an `if` statement.

rules.construct: Decorators on a function or method: `@property`.
rules.condition: Each decorator on a function is one of: `@property`, `@<name>.setter` or `@<name>.deleter` for a property defined in the same class, `@staticmethod`, `@classmethod`, or `@override` (imported from `typing`, or written as `@typing.override`). No other decorator is permitted.

rules.construct: A variadic positional parameter: `def f(*args)`.
rules.condition: A function may declare `*args` only if its body uses `args` only as `*args` in one call, passing the values on unchanged.

rules.construct: A variadic keyword parameter: `def f(**kwargs)`.
rules.condition: A function may declare `**kwargs` only if its body uses `kwargs` only as `**kwargs` in one call, passing the values on unchanged.

rules.construct: A function defined inside the body of another function.
rules.condition: A function body may contain a nested `def` only if the nested function does not use any name that is a parameter or a local variable of the enclosing function.

rules.construct: Keyword arguments in a class header: `class A(metaclass=Meta)`, `class B(Base, flag=True)`.
rules.replacement: Write the behaviour as explicit methods or as module-level functions. To check subclasses, call a check function explicitly after the class is defined.

rules.construct: The base classes listed in a class header: `class Child(Parent)`.
rules.condition: A class lists at most one base class.

rules.construct: Decorators on a class: `@dataclass`.
rules.condition: The only permitted class decorator is `@dataclass` or `@dataclasses.dataclass`, written with or without keyword arguments, such as `@dataclass(frozen=True)`.

rules.construct: Importing every public name from a module with `from module import *`.
rules.replacement: Import the names you use explicitly, or import the module and qualify each name.

rules.construct: Relative imports: `from . import sibling`, `from ..package import name`.
rules.condition: A relative import has at most one leading dot. Imports from parent packages use the absolute module path.

rules.construct: An `except` clause: `except ValueError as error:`.
rules.condition: Every `except` clause names the exception type or types it handles. A bare `except:` is not permitted.

rules.construct: The `try` statement with `except*` clauses for exception groups.
rules.replacement: Catch the `ExceptionGroup` with a normal `except` clause and inspect its `exceptions` attribute explicitly.

rules.construct: Coroutines and asynchronous statements: `async def`, `await`, `async for`, `async with`.
rules.replacement: Write synchronous code. If concurrency is necessary, keep it outside code that must conform to the subset until async rules exist.

rules.construct: An `async for` clause in a comprehension: `[x async for x in stream]`.
